text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.84% today, recovering from a sharp four-day slide that saw the stock drop 5.6% from $142.28 to $134.40 between November 13 and 18. The rebound appears tied to stabilizing oil prices and potential tailwinds for U.S. energy producers: crude is holding near $90 per barrel, and the Senate just passed a major permitting reform bill that would streamline project approvals for energy and AI infrastructure—a significant win for large integrated oil companies looking to expand operations.

The broader backdrop also turned somewhat supportive. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East continue to threaten oil supply routes (the IEA warned of lost confidence in the Strait of Hormuz), and Europe faces a sharp energy crunch heading into winter with depleted gas stocks and cold weather potentially driving up global energy demand. These structural pressures on energy supply, combined with the permitting reform momentum, likely helped reverse the stock's recent losses.
